claim: Masking is always on and no setting turns it off; when a result column's label matches a secret word, every value in that column including NULL is replaced with `[withheld]` before the result reaches the table, the model, the conversation history, the server log and the temp-directory result CSV, the column itself stays, and the model is told which columns were withheld.
source_excerpt: SQL Lens hides the values of secret-looking columns in every query result. Masking is always on; no setting turns it off. source_excerpt: | `unmasked_words` | list of strings | `[]` | Built-in entries to stop applying, for a database that uses one of them for ordinary data. claim: Labels and entries are split into words at every non-letter-non-digit character, at lowercase-to-uppercase changes, before the last capital of an uppercase run followed by lowercase letters, and between letters and digits, with one exception keeping an uppercase run plus a single lowercase `s` followed by a non-letter or end of label as one word; a label matches when its words contain all of an entry's words consecutively and in order, each word optionally carrying a trailing `s` or `es`.
source_excerpt: **How labels match.** SQL Lens splits a column label into words at every character that is not a letter or digit, at lowercase-to-uppercase changes, before the last capital of an uppercase run followed by lowercase letters, and between letters and digits (`password_hash` → password, hash; `APIKey` → api, key; `password2` → password, 2). One exception keeps a plural together: an uppercase run followed by a single lowercase `s` and then a non-letter or the end of the label stays one word (`PINs` → pins). Entries split the same way. A label matches when its words contain all of an entry's words, consecutively and in order; each word may also carry a trailing `s` or `es` (`api_keys`, `PINs`).
verify_against: The label word splitter and matching predicate
verify_hint: Check the word-splitting function and the entry-matching method of `SecretColumnMatcher` in `src/sqllens/safety/masking.py`, including the plural-`s` exception and the trailing `s`/`es` allowance

claim: This finding from the previous review no longer holds at the reviewed head: 9. In `docs/external/configuration.md` the bullet listing the cases masking misses reads "a secret column renamed by an alias (`password_hash AS h`), a view or a UNION branch label", which a reader can take to mean that a UNION branch label is never masked. A UNION whose first branch selects `password_hash` without an alias is labelled `password_hash` and is masked; only the renaming hides it. The sentence is true under the reading that "renamed by" governs all three cases, which is how the acceptance criterion phrases it too, so this is a clarity point. (raised by 1/6 agents)

prior_evidence: The docstring at tests/unit/test_factory_wiring.py:533-535 says that when enabled the read-only guard 'must sit directly beneath the masking guard'. In src/sqllens/agent/factory.py:93-109 the order is RowCap, then ReadOnlyGuardRunner (94), then, if cfg.rls is set, RlsGuardRunner (100-101), then ResultMaskingRunner (104).
